about: The moth's rig (docs/moth-5): one carbon mast, a boom, shrouds to the wings and a forestay, and one fully battened deck-sweeper film sail. Game frame for x and z (forward from the hull's middle, up from the design waterline), metres. Sizes from the size card (mast 5.1 m: the tuning guide's standard; back of mast to clew ring 2.34 m; shroud base 1.5 m; sail 8.25 m^2, its luff 5.04 m: from 4 cm over the deck to 2 cm under the masthead, inside the class's 5,185 mm). An invented sail: no builder's shape, logo or graphics.

mast.note: a two-piece carbon mast of a slim teardrop section in a step on the deck 0.4 m ahead of the main strut (Milestone A moved it forward from 0.47: the camera-matched flying photo and the bow-quarter photo put the mast about 0.29 of the hull length from the bow), raked aft 12 degrees (Milestone A raised it from 9: the matched photo fits 12 best, and four of six reviewers saw the photos' masts raked further back); the sail's luff sleeve goes over it, so its area is in the sail's (class rule 9.1: mast area inside the sail isn't added)

boom.note: back of the mast to the clew ring 2.34 m (the tuning guide); a deck-sweeper's boom rides high, the sail's foot below it sweeps down to the deck

sail.note: luff along the mast's back from the tack (4 cm over the deck: the deck-sweeper's foot) to the head; a square top (Milestone A: every photo shows a wide head, about a quarter of the foot); leech from the head out over a full roach to the clew at the boom's end; the foot curves from the tack down along the deck and up to the clew. roach scales the leech's bulge; the build solves it to the card's 8.25 m^2 Milestone B widened the head 0.65 to 0.85 m: five of six reviewers over rounds 1 and 2 read the top as narrow, nearly a triangle, next to the photos' square tops; at 0.92 two of three in round 3 read it as too wide, so it settles between; the roach is solved to the area again.

spreaders.note: one pair of spreaders swept aft at 1.9 m, about 37% of the mast (Milestone A round 2: all three reviewers put the photos' spreaders at 35-40%), the shrouds over their tips (Milestone A: all three reviewers saw them in the photos)

rigging.note: two shrouds from the hounds to the wings' front bars (ShroudBase, 0.75 m out) and a forestay to the deck near the bow
